text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs delivered a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with a standard deviation of 2.14%. The distribution is slightly right-skewed at 0.51, but 52% of the analogs finished below zero, making the single anchor for this state a near-flat outcome with wide dispersion rather than a directional edge.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 28 distinct sessions across 22 symbols because the current state is defined by three unusual features. First, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, meaning liquidity has dried up significantly versus history. Second, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, a sharp energy move. Third, 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed to 9.16%. These features carry heavy weight in the retrieval: dv20z, vol20, and oilChg20 sit inside the name and macro groups which together account for 50% of the distance metric. The combination of low volume, low volatility, and a large oil shock pulls recent broad ETF sessions—particularly from 2025 and 2026—into the nearest neighborhood.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced returns ranging from -5.12% to 6.88%. The mean was -0.03% and the median was -0.1%. The 10th percentile was -2.39% and the 90th percentile was 3.29%. The histogram shows the bulk of outcomes clustered between -1.37% and 1.13%, with 48% of episodes finishing above zero and 52% below. The bad tail is dominated by recent broad-market weakness. The closest analog, IWM on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2997), fell -2.98% over five sessions. JPM on 2026-09-04 (distance 0.3418) dropped -2.37%, and DIA on 2026-09-02 (distance 0.3258) lost -1.86%. SPY itself appears in the set: on 2026-09-03 (distance 0.3101) it returned -1.15%, while an older SPY episode on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.3366) rallied 3.47%. The worst single outcome in the full set was -5.12%, though the specific symbol and date for that minimum are not isolated in the top-12 list.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. At the 10th percentile, the path dipped -3.1% before recovering, and the 25th percentile adverse excursion was -1.98%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%, with the 90th percentile reaching 3.52%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 0.94. Looking at drawdown breaches during the 5 sessions, 4% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown threshold. Zero analogs breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown.

[stress]
The baseline median across all 50 analogs is -0.1%. Several stress scenarios materially worsen that picture. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario used 48 analogs and produced a median forward return of -4.61%, a delta of -4.51% versus baseline, with a 41.7% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, and it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock used 26 analogs, yielding a median of -0.92% (delta -0.82%) and a 23.1% probability of a 10% drawdown breach; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation / rate bear used 50 analogs for a median of -2.09% (delta -1.99%) and a 2% breach probability; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare used 50 analogs, returning a median of -1.09% (delta -0.99%) with a 0% breach probability; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The earnings release day shock used 50 analogs for a median of -0.79% (delta -0.69%) and a 2% breach probability; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than the 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind used 36 analogs, returning a median of -0.49% (delta -0.39%) with a 2.8% breach probability; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) used 50 analogs for a median of -0.2% (delta -0.1%) and a 4% breach probability; caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket used 50 analogs for a median of -0.13% (delta -0.03%) and a 4% breach probability; caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not on a 7x24 venue, and when a tokenised wrapper for this instrument was verified, 61.18% of its realised hourly movement happened in closed hours, so the gap risk described is not hypothetical. Scenarios that improved the picture include the 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 1.41%, delta 1.51%, 36 analogs; caveat: very short window, analog set dominated by a handful of sessions), crypto drawdown contagion (median 0.77%, delta 0.87%, 50 analogs; caveat: BTC feature is a market-wide proxy, name-level linkage not identified), China ADR de-rating (median 0.16%, delta 0.26%, 50 analogs; caveat: delisting risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space), policy-rate path re-pricing (median 0.07%, delta 0.17%, 50 analogs; caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, transmission depends on duration not captured here), FOMC decision day (median -0.11%, delta -0.01%, 50 analogs; caveat: only 92 decision days exist, analog set is small and highly overlapping), and weekend hold on the 7x24 venue (median -0.21%, delta -0.11%, 50 analogs; caveat: blocks are paired by index modulo block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution). No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because the current state's defining feature is a -1.985 dv20z reading, and that scenario shows what happens when liquidity dries up further, producing a -4.61% median across 48 analogs with a 41.7% chance of a 10% drawdown breach. Second is the 2025-04 tariff shock, because the 19.24% oilChg20 points to a commodity-driven policy sensitivity, and this scenario captures discrete trade shocks, yielding a -0.92% median across 26 analogs with a 23.1% breach probability. Third is the 2022 inflation / rate bear, because the combination of compressed vol20 at 9.16% and a large oil move historically preceded multiple compression, resulting in a -2.09% median across 50 analogs. A concentration to distrust is the heavy weighting of 2025 (26 analogs) and 2026 (14 analogs) in the retrieval, alongside 18 ETF Broad matches out of 50 total, meaning the distribution is largely describing the last two years of broad-market behavior rather than a diverse historical base. No scenario contradicts the direction implied by the baseline median of -0.1%; the positive-delta scenarios simply show regimes where this specific state resolved favorably.

[limits]
This analysis retrieves historical conditional distributions, not forecasts. The honestVerdict states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Out of sample, the conformal interval achieved 80.8% coverage against an 80% target, but the directional hit rate was only 50.1%, and the PIT chi-square was 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the distribution fails uniformity. For path risk, the engine predicted a mean breach probability of 3.4% for a 10% drawdown, but the realised breach rate out of sample was 2%, leaving a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score was 0.0196, beating the volatility reflection benchmark (0.0241), the same-name calibration (0.024), and the pooled calibration (0.021). The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve these differences: the 95% CI versus vol reflection is [-0.0071, -0.0022], versus same-name is [-0.0059, -0.0029], and versus pooled is [-0.0023, -0.0005]; none span zero, so the analog's superiority in Brier score is statistically resolved in all three cases. The wrapper status is measured. On the primary Bitget venue (SPY/USDT perpetual), the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, yet 61.18% of the wrapper's realised hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9477 and a tracking error of 23 bp/day. The basis band is -0.04% to 0.31%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. Caveat: a fair perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis means exit prices differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. For the return layer, measured across 6 weekend blocks on Bitget, the median weekend block return was -0.101%, the 10th percentile was -0.506%, and the standard deviation was 0.4191%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.2125%, and 0% of weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
